subject: McGlynn and Andrews Schools HVAC Project
overview: The committee approved a $5 million initial bond request for major HVAC replacements at the McGlynn and Andrews schools and reviewed a multi-year district capital plan. The meeting also included the recognition of multiple championship-winning athletic teams and the marching band.

items.title: Executive Session
items.summary: The committee entered executive session to discuss collective bargaining strategy regarding negotiations with the Massachusetts Teachers Association.

items.title: Consent Agenda
items.summary: Approved routine items including bills, payrolls, field trips, meeting minutes, and a $750 grant for the McGlynn Elementary School library.

items.title: Superintendent's Report
items.summary: Superintendent Edouard-Vincent announced her January 17 departure date, recognized a $60,000 donation of musical instruments from Music Drives Us, and shared updates on kindergarten registration.

items.title: Introduction of District Assistance Dog
items.summary: Director Stacey Shulman introduced Kelsey, a certified assistance dog trained to provide behavioral health support to students and staff.

items.title: Student Achievement Recognitions
items.summary: The committee honored several fall sports teams and athletes for Greater Boston League championships and individual MVP awards, as well as the NESBA Division II champion marching band.

items.title: HVAC Project Approval and Bond Recommendation
items.summary: Approved the McGlynn and Andrews HVAC project and recommended that the City Council authorize an initial $5 million bond for design and early equipment procurement. The project aims to restore classroom cooling by the start of the 2025 school year to address failed systems and obsolete refrigerants.

items.title: Revised Budget Calendar
items.summary: Approved a revised development timeline for the FY26 budget to allow more time for leadership review and narrative development.

items.title: District Capital Plan Review
items.summary: Approved a comprehensive capital plan detailing prioritized maintenance and infrastructure needs, including ADA compliance, roof assessments, and security upgrades. The committee referred the plan to the administration to be considered in an upcoming supplemental budget request.
